page: Microsoft Azure M64-16ms is a memory-intensive server instance belonging to the MS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading operating at 2.7 GHz. The processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1D cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX, AVX512F, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA.

A defining characteristic of this server is its massive memory capacity of 1792.0 GB, yielding an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio of 112.0 GB per core. It is equipped with 2097 GB of local SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance tradeoff. Single-core performance is consistently limited, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded compression tasks scoring in the bottom 10 percent. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by average ratings in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks remains average, though the Passmark memory score falls into the bottom 25 percent.

Given its hardware profile, the M64-16ms is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring massive memory footprints relative to compute power, avoiding the expense of provisioning excess vCPUs just to acquire RAM. It is well-suited for large in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, and memory-heavy database operations. It is less suitable for compute-bound single-threaded tasks or medium-to-large LLM inference.
